transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because I just can't seem to shake this feeling that work isn't safe anymore. And... I don't know, I just feel like I'm somehow damaged now. Like the competent person who got promoted just isn't really there anymore.
Can you tell me more about this feeling that work isn't safe anymore?

Well, I just... I try to avoid being there in certain situations now. I have some flexibility, so I've started trading shifts with coworkers, or pushing back on our release windows. I just work from home whenever I possibly can. 

And if I do have to actually go into the office, I always take the side entrance now. I just can't... I mean, walking through that main lobby after dark just makes me feel like I’m going to completely come apart.
Did something specific happen at work that made you start feeling this way?
Yes. There was a break-in at the building. It happened during an overnight deployment I was working on... that was about two years and four months ago. This has all been going on ever since then.
Are there any other places or situations, outside of work, that you avoid because they make you feel anxious or uncomfortable?

No, not really. I mean... I think it's mostly just tied to work. Outside of that, I don't really avoid anywhere else. I still go out to run errands or see friends and I feel okay. 

It's really just the office, or I guess being alone in a big commercial building at night. But in my normal, personal life... no, I haven't noticed anything like that.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the break-in at the building in your mind?

Yeah, I do. It doesn't take much to set it off, honestly. Just hearing a badge scanner beep, or... heavy footsteps out in the hallway. Even just getting a late-night deployment alert on my phone can do it. 

When that happens, it just suddenly puts me right back in that office. My chest gets completely tight, and I just see the image of the guard on the floor... it just cuts right through whatever I’m trying to do in that moment.
Do you try to avoid thinking or talking about the break-in at your office?

Yeah, I do. I try not to talk about it or even think about it if I can help it. It's actually gotten to the point where I avoid anything that brings it up... I’ve started trading shifts and pushing back on my release windows just so I don't have to be in those situations. 

I just work from home whenever I can now. And if I absolutely have to go into the office, I take the side entrance... because just walking through that main lobby after dark makes me feel like I’m going to come apart. So, yeah, I basically do whatever I can to avoid dealing with it.
Do you often find yourself being easily startled by small things?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I don't feel like I jump at small noises or get startled easily... unless it's something that specifically reminds me of the office, like I mentioned before. But just in general day-to-day things? No, I don't think so.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself, or like things aren't real?

No, I don't think I've ever felt anything quite like that. I always feel like I'm... you know, right here, in my own body. Things feel real to me, just sometimes really overwhelming when those memories hit. But I haven't had that feeling of watching myself from the outside or anything.
Do you often feel guilty about what happened during the break-in at your office?

Yeah, I do. Um... I keep thinking that if I had just insisted on better security for that overnight deployment, or maybe if I had called for help sooner... the guard might not have been hurt so badly. 

I mean, logically, part of me knows that I was just hiding and I was completely terrified, but... yeah. I still blame myself a lot for how it all turned out.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family since the break-in?

Um... no, not really. Things with my friends and family are pretty much the same. I still see them and talk to them like I usually do. I mean, they know what happened and they've been supportive, but I haven't really noticed any changes in how we get along or anything.
Has your ability to do your job or take care of daily responsibilities been significantly impacted by these feelings and memories?

Yes, it definitely has. My work has really slipped lately. I've actually missed a few migration deadlines, and I've been completely avoiding any key late-night deployments because of what happened. It's gotten to the point where my manager brought it up in a recent performance review. I've also been having some conflicts with coworkers, which never used to happen before. 

Outside of my day-to-day work, I've also pulled back from mentoring and the women-in-tech leadership events I used to be involved in. I just don't feel steady or reliable enough to do those things anymore.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Um... no, not really. I mean, other than stepping back from the mentoring and the leadership events like I mentioned, I still do the things I usually like to do. I still read, I still go to the gym... I haven't really lost interest in my hobbies or anything like that.
Do you often think that you're permanently changed for the worse because of what happened during the break-in?

Yeah, I do. I honestly can't shake the feeling that I'm somehow damaged now. It's like... the competent person who got promoted just isn't really there anymore. And I also have this constant feeling that work just isn't safe anymore. That's really why I'm here talking to you, because I just can't seem to get past that.
Have you experienced any difficulties in your personal relationships since the break-in?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues there. I mean, like I said earlier, I've had some friction with my coworkers, but outside of work... my personal relationships are fine. My friends and family have been pretty supportive, so nothing has really changed on that front.
Do you try to avoid feeling emotions related to the break-in, such as anxiety or fear?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I definitely feel the anxiety and fear, but I don't think I try to block those feelings out or avoid them. They just sort of... happen, and I feel them. I haven't really been doing anything to try and push those emotions away.
Do you ever feel numb or detached from the world around you?

No, I don't think so. I definitely don't feel numb. If anything, I feel things pretty strongly right now, especially the anxiety I mentioned. But I don't feel detached from the world or anything like that. I'm still pretty tuned in to what's going on around me.
